claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or nanoribbons exhibit significant chemical disorder.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or nanoribbons exhibit internal strain heterogeneity.
Chemical disorder and deposition-induced strain heterogeneity enhance local magnetic anisotropy.
Chemical disorder and strain heterogeneity increase domain-wall pinning.
Magnetic inhomogeneity broadens magnetic hysteresis in the nanoscale alloy.
Magnetic inhomogeneity reduces the effective low-field magnetocaloric response of nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi relative to bulk material.
Heat-transfer limitations in the nanoscale geometry constrain thermal equilibration and usable cycle frequency.
Sub-melting pulse laser annealing can promote partial chemical ordering in the alloy.
Sub-melting pulse laser annealing can relieve internal stresses without significantly changing the nanoscale dimensions.
Increased local chemical order and reduced strain lower strain-induced interface anisotropy.
Reduced interface anisotropy and strain produce fewer effective domain-wall pinning sites.
Reduced magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall pinning narrow hysteresis loops and reduce coercivity.
Reduced disorder, stress, anisotropy, and pinning increase the adiabatic temperature change during low-field magnetocaloric cycling.
Improved local chemical ordering may marginally increase thermal conductivity.
A marginal increase in thermal conductivity reduces thermal-equilibration delays during rapid cycling.
The predicted effects apply at applied magnetic fields below 0.1 T and at temperatures near the magnetic transition.
Surface and strain effects dominate the behavior at the relevant nanoscale dimensions.
Increasing the dimensions substantially or causing grain coarsening through excessive annealing may invalidate the predicted response.
